data.name: Epic Cards Battle(TCG)
data.detailed_description:
Jogo de Cartão de Negociação Estratégica em 3D (TCG) que você não pode perder!

Batalha de Cartões Épicas permití-lo experimentar batalhas lendárias com amigos e jogadores de todo o mundo!
Características

- O jogo de batalha de cartões Revolucionárias de Geração Próxima em 3D está com centenas de efeitos visuais de batalha impressionante. Os jogadores vão realmente experimentar as batalhas épicas que acontecem na frente deles.

- Abandona os jogos de cartões sem cérebro e começa a jogar o jogo verdadeiro de cartões estratégicas, 3 modelos de tipos de cartões: Unidade, Magia, Gatilho. Construa a sua própria plataforma de cartões para conquistar o seu adversário.

- Livre de despesa- para jogar: Os jogadores podiam desfrutar da diversão sem gastar um centavo.

- Experiência a tomada de jogo em tempo real e batalha com jogadores de todo o mundo.

- Os sistemas de jogo bem desenhados. Escada, quadros de líderes
, o sistema de saque de cartões, recompensas de entrada diária, missões diárias, reforço de cartões, repetições de batalha, amigos, sistema de bate-papo.

- Missões da campanha com muitas recompensas, cada missão é cuidadosamente desenhada para ser um enigma esperando para se desafiar.

- 5 facções principais: Aliança Santuário, Força da Natureza, Legião de Inferno, Império de Fanstiya, nascente de dinastia. 5 alvos de ataque, 4 tipos de ataque e 4 tipos de armadura. Combinações ilimitadas de cartõe
s, empurrando os limites do seu cérebro.

- Fácil de jogar e difícil de dominar. Você pode começar imediatamente sem saber todas as regras de batalha. Tutoriais interativos ajudarão você a obter o conhecimento básico deste jogo rapidamente.

- Suporta batalha sincronizada que permite que você jogue com os amigos a qualquer hora, você não tem que esperar amigo que será no internet.

- Interface incrível de jogo, obras de arte e a música das trilhas sonoras lendário inspirá-lo enquanto está a jogar.

(Suporta várias linguagens no jogo)

reviews.review:
Epic Cards Battle(TCG) is an older free to play card game that surprised me with how much strategy is actually packed into it. At first it looks like a fairly simple fantasy card game, but once I start getting into the deck building and combat systems there is quite a bit more to think about. I build a deck using Units, Spells and Triggers, then try to work out how the different cards and effects can work together. The battles play out automatically once the cards are set up, so a lot of the actual strategy comes from what I put into my deck and how I prepare for different situations.

The faction system gives me plenty of room to experiment. There are five main factions, and the game also has different attack targets, attack types and armour types that affect how battles work. I like this because it stops deck building from being completely obvious. I have to think about what I am trying to counter and how my cards are going to interact rather than simply filling my deck with the strongest looking cards. It takes some time to understand all of the systems, but once I get used to them I can see why the game has more depth than its fairly dated presentation suggests.

The campaign is probably the part I enjoy most when I want to play on my own. The quests are designed more like little puzzles than simple fights, so I have to work out which cards and combinations can get me through certain situations. There are also daily missions, rewards, card looting and card enhancement, which give me plenty of reasons to keep progressing. The ladder and other battle modes add another layer when I want something more competitive, while asynchronous battles are useful because I do not have to be playing at exactly the same time as someone else.

The 3D presentation is also quite unusual for a card game from this period. When the cards start attacking, there are a lot of effects happening on the battlefield, and I like seeing the units actually come to life instead of everything staying as flat cards on a table. The artwork has that older fantasy and anime style, which is not always going to work for me, but it gives the game a clear identity. The soundtrack and battle effects also make the fights feel more active than the underlying mechanics might suggest.

The biggest problem for me is the age of the game. Some parts of the interface feel dated, and there is a lot of information that I have to learn before the more complicated systems start making sense. The progression can also feel like a grind because I am collecting cards, enhancing them and working towards stronger decks over time. I do not mind grinding when it is helping me build something interesting, but there are moments where I feel like I am spending more time improving my collection than actually making meaningful strategic decisions.

The free to play structure is something I can appreciate more than I expected. The game has a lot of systems built around rewards, daily activities and card progression, but the core game is available without requiring me to spend money. There are in app purchases, so I still have to be aware of that side of the design, but I like that there is a proper campaign and plenty of progression to work through without paying. The sheer number of systems also gives me quite a lot to explore for an older free game.

Overall, Epic Cards Battle(TCG) is much deeper than I expected from a free card game that was released back in 2015. I like the deck building, different card types, factions, campaign puzzles, card enhancement and the amount of strategy hidden in the combat system. The dated interface, grinding and fairly complicated learning curve stop it from being one of my highest rated card games, but there is enough here to keep me interested once I understand how everything fits together. For me, it works best when I take the time to learn the systems instead of expecting a quick and simple card game.

Rating: 7/10
